chunks: And Al-Hasan ibn 'Abdillah narrated to me from Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from his father, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from 'Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Al-Halabi, who said:

I heard Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) say: Al-Husayn (peace be upon him) led his companions in the morning prayer, then turned to them and said, 'Verily, Allah has granted permission for your killing, so upon you is patience.'

key_terms.الْحُسَيْنُ (ع): Imam Al-Husayn, peace be upon him

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Husayn say to his companions after leading the morning prayer on the Day of Ashura?
ai.summary: Recorded in Ibn Qulawayh’s *Kamil al-Ziyarat*, this hadith highlights the spiritual fortitude of Imam al-Husayn (a.s.) as he led the morning prayer before facing his fate. By stating that Allah had 'permitted' their death, he framed the martyrdom not as a defeat but as a divine decree, urging his companions to respond with *sabr* (steadfast patience), a concept deeply rooted in Shia theology as an active, conscious endurance of divine will.

en.sayyid-mohsen-al-husayni-al-milani: 8. Ḥasan ibn ‘Abdillāh ibn Muḥammad ibn ‘Isā narrated to me from his father, from Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb, from ‘Ali ibn Ri`āb, from Al-Ḥalabi, who said:

I heard Abā ‘Abdillāh (Imam Sādiq (a.s.)) say: Ḥusain (a.s.) led the Fajr prayer (on the Day of ‘Āshūrā) for his companions and then turned back toward them and said, “Verily Allāh has granted permission for you to be killed, so remain patient.”
